notes:
Key account notes:
- Primary contact: CTO (Anita Rao) — heavy focus on tail latency and reproducible measurement.
- Goal: move core chat/reranking to Redwood Dedicated with hard latency SLOs and reserved GPU pools.
- Quote from technical call: "We need deterministic tails — p99 under 250ms for non-streaming responses at baseline traffic."
- They use TLS-terminated load balancers in front of client apps; want guidance on measuring client-side vs server-side times.
- Decided to split SLOs: non-streaming: p50/p95/p99 measured at server ingress-to-last-token; streaming: time-to-first-token (TTFT) p50/p95 and time-to-complete p99. Also want client-side wall-clock comparisons for network variance.
- Proposed measurement definitions (agreed provisional):
  * Non-streaming latency = server_receive_timestamp -> server_last_byte_timestamp (server-side). Target: p50 30ms, p95 120ms, p99 250ms for short prompts (~64 tokens).
  * Streaming TF-first = server_receive_timestamp -> server_first_token_timestamp. Target: p50 12ms, p95 45ms.
  * Client-side measurement = client_send_timestamp -> client_last_token_received_timestamp. Expect ~20–60ms added depending on region/network; will report both views in dashboards.
- Concern: batching and KV cache reuse will change latency distributions; POC will include cold-cache run vs warmed-cache run.
- Throughput/Reserved planning: they expect sustained 1,200 requests/sec (embeddings mixed) with 200 concurrent chat sessions; ask for guidance on GPU sizing, autoscale headroom, and SLA credits for degradation.
- Rules-of-thumb agreed: treat streaming and non-streaming as separate SLO buckets; include 95th-98th percentile of time-to-first-token for interactive use.
- Stakeholders: CTO, Head of Platform (engineering), GRC lead, Procurement.
